sentences.text: Laganosuchus is an extinct type of crocodyliform belonging to the family Stomatosuchidae.
Scientists know about this animal only from the lower jaws of two different species.
One species had a jaw measuring 838 mm in length, holding twenty-four simple, straight spikes on each side.
Researchers named the creature 'PancakeCroc' because its skull was unusually shallow, resembling a pancake.
This fish-eating predator reached a massive size, growing up to six meters long with a one-meter-wide flat head.
Paul Sereno and Hans Larsson first described the genus in 2009.
Fossil remains have been recovered from the regions of Niger and Morocco.
The weak symphysis, which is the joint where the two halves of the lower jaw meet, suggests the animal had a very weak bite.
Despite the weak bite force, the tightly fitting nature of the teeth would have prevented fish from escaping once trapped.
It is debated whether Laganosuchus possessed gular sacs beneath its throat, as there is no fossil evidence to confirm or deny this feature.
These animals lived during the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
